name: furniture-design
description: Furniture designs and the published knowledge they are judged against. Kinds: source and clause (a publication and its verbatim, located statements, with the quantities they state), material (properties derived from clauses), requirement (a demand resting on clauses, with its limits and test conditions), piece, part and load. Rules: every clause quotes its source; requirements and materials rest on clauses; a piece in a requirement's scope is held to it; a piece stands in its stability cases (furniture/tipping_cases); a part bends within its longtime sag limit (Wood Handbook Eq. 9-2 to 9-4 and its creep guidance, furniture/deflection, with no shear term for a panel whose modulus was measured on the panel); a part is strong enough (Eq. 9-13 against the near-minimum modulus of rupture over the Handbook's factor for 10-year duration of load and safety); a part bends the way its material's values were measured; a seat carries the light-service sidethrust of GSA's FNAE-80-214A through a panel in the push's plane (furniture/sideways_margin); a part that swells and shrinks with the air has room to (Eq. 13-3, the moisture content of its climate from Eq. 4-5, kind climate), and is judged only where that equation holds; a joint is cut with a tool its connector takes, at its setting, in parts thick and wide enough for it (kinds tool, connector, joint; a maker's products are data in a package of their own); a part with cuts is cut with tools that rest on clauses saying how they are used; a part is cut out of its board with saws that state, from their makers' clauses, the width they take out (which the cutting sheet leaves between parts) and that cut through each of its sheets. The rules carry no number a source states: limits and properties are read from the knowledge base. Every published shelf and beam deflection limit found is a clause a design chooses its own sag limit from; none is a requirement every part is held to.

vocabulary.description: A publication the knowledge base quotes: payload title-like name, publisher, year, identifier, url, sha256 of what was fetched, licence (public-domain, cc-by-4.0, copyrighted, or unstated when it could not be established) and, when the licence allows (public-domain, cc-by-4.0), capture (the path of the text kept in the repo). Its children are the clauses quoted from it.

A located statement of its parent source: payload locator (chapter, table, page) and quote (verbatim); transcribed when the statement is an equation or a table row text extraction cannot read, read from the page and marked as transcription. A clause of a copyrighted source carries its locator and no quote: the words are the publisher's, and the copy they can be checked against is kept where it may be. Its params are the quantities it states, converted to SI, provenance published; rows, when present, say for each where it is printed: [param, the words it follows, the value as printed, the number, how it becomes SI]. A deflection limit states share_of_span (the deflection over the span), max_deflection (mm), surface_load (kg/m2), load_duration (h) or creep_factor (final over initial deflection), and in payload what it applies_to, when the deflection is measured and under which load.

params.(any): a quantity the clause states, in SI, its original wording in note

vocabulary.description: A material a part is made of. Its params are its properties, each derived_from the clauses it was computed from; a part links to it with `uses` and reads them as its own. payload form (solid wood, plywood, ...), measured_along (the direction its bending values were measured in: grain; face grain, flat; across face grain, flat (plywood bent with its face grain across the span); major axis, flat and minor axis, flat (OSB, along and across the panel's length); flat (a board with no grain in its plane: particleboard, MDF, hardboard); or unstated when the source does not say) and modulus (true: corrected for shear deflection, so a shear term is added; apparent: measured on the panel with its shear deflection in it).

params.modulus_of_elasticity: EL, MPa (for a panel, its bending modulus as tested on the panel)
params.modulus_of_rupture: MPa, the mean bending strength the source states
params.design_bending_stress: MPa, the bending stress a part may be designed to
params.initial_share_of_longtime: the share of a permitted longtime deflection the initial deflection may reach (creep)
params.screw_withdrawal_face: N, the force that pulls a screw out of the panel's face; its note names the test and the screw
params.screw_withdrawal_edge: N, the same from the panel's edge; its note names the test and the screw
params.thickness_swelling_24h: %, how much the panel thickens after 24 h in water (EN 317)
params.dimensional_change_in_plane: 1/%, the change in length in the panel's plane per 1% change in moisture content

links.per: the clauses its properties come from

vocabulary.description: A demand a design can be checked against: payload measure (what it limits, e.g. overturning, longtime_sag), scope {category} when it applies to a category of piece, and the test conditions in words; params its limits and test conditions, and min_<x> for a scope threshold on the piece's x (height, mass, or a param the piece carries). A design may author its own requirement (a target it sets itself), provenance design-target.

params.limit: the largest value the measure may take
params.min_<x>: the piece is in scope only when its x reaches this

vocabulary.description: A piece of furniture: its parts beneath it. Frame: x across, y from the front (smallest y) to the back, z up from the floor, mm. payload category (e.g. clothing-storage-unit) brings it into a requirement's scope.

params.storage_volume: mm3, what it holds, when a requirement's scope reads it

links.stability_case: the overturning requirements it is held to
links.sideways_case: the sideways-force requirements it is held to
links.braced_by: the panels standing in the plane of a sideways force (a back), joined along their top and side edges, that carry it to the floor

vocabulary.description: A component to make. payload shape {op: box, size: [x, y, z]} in mm, transform {translate} placing its minimum corner relative to the enclosing part or piece (geometry@'s convention), each entry a number or an expression over params (the part's own, then those of the parts and piece holding it, nearest first), so a dimension the piece states once moves every part that depends on it; extends (mm it opens towards the front) for a drawer or pull-out shelf; hinged for a door (not modelled yet); span_along (grain, face grain) for a part that bends: the way its grain runs along its span; shear_modulus naming the material property that is G for it (shear_modulus_lr for a board whose vertical faces are edge-grained, the common flat-sawn board lying flat; shear_modulus_lt for flat-grained vertical faces). A part that bends names its span, depth and thickness params and its Table 9-1 case. A part that swells and shrinks with the air (a floating panel) links the climate it lives in and its movement equation, names in payload across_grain the param that is its width across the grain and in dimensional_change the material property that moves it (dimensional_change_tangential for a flat-sawn face, dimensional_change_radial for a quartersawn one), and states the clearance it has. payload cuts: what is taken out of the board, a list of boxes {at, size} in the part's own frame (each entry a number or an expression over params, as for its size), such as a notch for a skirting board; a part's cuts are not a joint's `cut`, which names the kind of connector seat. A part with cuts links made_with the tools that cut them, each saying how it is used and resting on clauses; the documents draw each cut measured from the edges it touches and number its saw lines in order. A part links sawn_with the saws that cut it out of its board: each must cut as deep as one of its sheets is thick and state the width it takes out, which the cutting sheet leaves between parts.

params.mass: kg, when it is not its volume times its material's density
params.thickness: mm, the beam's depth h, and a joined panel's thickness
params.clearance: mm the part may grow across the grain before it is stopped

links.bends_as: the Table 9-1 clause for its loading and supports
links.sag_limit: the longtime-sag requirements it is held to
links.moves_per: the clause of the movement equation it is judged by
links.made_with: the tools that cut its cuts
links.sawn_with: the saws that cut it out of its board

vocabulary.description: A machine, jig or hand tool that cuts or drills what a part or a joint needs: payload maker, what it does (does) and, for a saw, saw_kind (hand saw, pull saw, jigsaw, circular saw, plunge saw, table saw, mitre saw, panel saw). A design names the tools it is made with; a connector names the tools that can cut its seat. A saw's params, each derived from a clause its maker printed: kerf (mm, the width the blade it comes with takes out), max_kerf (mm, the widest blade it takes, when its maker states no blade's), blade_thickness (mm, the blade's body: a kerf is wider), max_cut_depth (mm, the thickest board it cuts through square).

params.kerf: mm, the width its blade takes out
params.max_kerf: mm, the widest blade it takes
params.max_cut_depth: mm, the thickest board it cuts through at 90°

links.per: the clauses that say what it does and its limits

vocabulary.description: A manufactured element that joins parts (a knock-down fitting, a biscuit, a dowel): payload maker and setting (the machine setting its seat is cut at, when it has one); params its limits — min_width (mm, the narrowest part it may join), min_thickness_<cut> (mm, per kind of cut: edge, surface, intermediate, mitre), pull_out_<material> and shear_<material> (N), moment_opening_<material> and moment_closing_<material> (N mm: one connector's share of what a corner joint resists being bent open or shut) — each derived from a clause; and its size as its maker states it, length (mm, along the joint) and thickness (mm, across it), which the documents draw it at.

params.moment_opening_<material>: N mm, one connector's share of what a corner joint resists being bent open
params.moment_closing_<material>: N mm, the same, bent shut
params.length: mm, the connector's length along the joint
params.thickness: mm, its thickness across the joint

links.needs: the tools that can cut its seat; any one of them will do
links.per: the clauses its limits come from

vocabulary.description: Where parts are joined. Links joins (the parts), uses (the connector it is made with, whose limits it reads as its own) and made_with (the tools that cut it); payload cut (edge, surface, intermediate or mitre: which of the connector's min_thickness_<cut> applies), setting (the machine setting it is cut at) and, when the design places its connectors, positions (mm along the longer side of the face the parts meet on; otherwise they are spread evenly, for the checks and the documents alike); param count (connectors in it). A joined part states its width and thickness.

links.made_with: the tools it is cut with

vocabulary.description: The air a piece lives in: params temperature (°C) and rh_min and rh_max, the driest and dampest relative humidity it sees, as decimals; a design states it (design-target) or a home measures it. It links emc_per to the equation that turns it into the moisture content wood settles at (furniture/emc).
Something a part carries: param mass (kg), payload distribution (uniform or a point), provenance published when a clause states it, design-target when the design does.

rules.name: a-clause-quotes-its-source
rules.expr: some(s, nodes('source'), s == parent(self)) and len(payload(self, 'locator', '')) > 0 and (len(payload(self, 'quote', '')) > 0 or payload(parent(self), 'licence', '') == 'copyrighted' or payload(parent(self), 'licence', '') == 'unstated')
rules.description: A clause sits under the source it comes from, says where in it, and quotes it, unless the source is copyrighted, or its licence could not be established (unstated): then it carries the values and the locator, and the words stay with their publisher.

rules.name: a-connector-rests-on-clauses
rules.expr: len(linked(self, 'per')) > 0 and every(c, linked(self, 'per'), some(k, nodes('clause'), k == c))
rules.description: A connector links `per` to the clauses its limits come from.

rules.name: a-joined-part-is-thick-enough-for-the-cut
rules.expr: every(p, linked(self, 'joins'), param(p, 'thickness') >= param(self, 'min_thickness_' + payload(self, 'cut')))
rules.description: Every part a joint joins is at least as thick as its connector allows for the kind of cut the joint is (the connector's min_thickness_<cut>, read through `uses`).

rules.name: a-joined-part-is-wide-enough
rules.expr: every(p, linked(self, 'joins'), param(p, 'width') >= param(self, 'min_width'))
rules.description: Every part a joint joins is at least as wide as its connector allows.

rules.name: a-joint-is-cut-with-a-tool-its-connector-takes
rules.expr: len(linked(self, 'made_with')) > 0 and every(c, linked(self, 'uses'), some(t, linked(c, 'needs'), some(m, linked(self, 'made_with'), m == t)))
rules.description: A joint names the tools it is cut with, and one of them is a tool its connector's seat can be cut with.

rules.name: a-joint-is-cut-at-its-connectors-setting
rules.expr: every(c, linked(self, 'uses'), payload(c, 'setting', '') == '' or payload(self, 'setting', '') == payload(c, 'setting', ''))
rules.description: When a connector's seat is cut at a machine setting, the joint says it is cut at that setting.

rules.name: a-part-with-cuts-is-cut-with-tools-that-rest-on-clauses
rules.expr: len(payload(self, 'cuts', '')) == 0 or (len(linked(self, 'made_with')) > 0 and every(t, linked(self, 'made_with'), len(linked(t, 'per')) > 0))
rules.description: A part with cuts names the tools that cut them, and each of those tools rests on clauses that say how it is used, so the instructions tell how to make the cut and not only where it is.

rules.name: a-part-is-sawn-with-a-saw-that-states-its-cut
rules.expr: every(t, linked(self, 'sawn_with'), (states(t, 'kerf') or states(t, 'max_kerf')) and len(linked(t, 'per')) > 0)
rules.description: Every saw a part is cut out with states the width it takes out (the kerf of its blade, or the widest blade it takes) and rests on the clauses it is read from, so the cutting sheet leaves between parts what that saw removes and not a guess. A saw whose maker prints neither is measured, and the measure stated on a saw of the design's own.

rules.name: a-part-is-no-thicker-than-its-saw-cuts
rules.expr: every(t, linked(self, 'sawn_with'), not states(t, 'max_cut_depth') or param(self, 'thickness') / payload(self, 'sheets', 1) <= param(t, 'max_cut_depth'))
rules.description: Each sheet of a part (its thickness over the sheets glued into it) is no thicker than every saw it is cut out with cuts through at 90°, as that saw's maker states it.

rules.name: a-requirement-rests-on-clauses
rules.expr: len(linked(self, 'per')) > 0 and every(c, linked(self, 'per'), some(k, nodes('clause'), k == c))
rules.description: A requirement links `per` to the clauses it rests on, and each is a clause in the tree; a target a design sets itself still names the clause that makes it a sensible measure.

rules.name: a-material-rests-on-clauses
rules.expr: len(linked(self, 'per')) > 0 and every(c, linked(self, 'per'), some(k, nodes('clause'), k == c))
rules.description: A material links `per` to the clauses its properties come from.

rules.name: a-load-acts-on-a-part
rules.expr: len(linked(self, 'on')) > 0 and every(p, linked(self, 'on'), some(k, nodes('part'), k == p))
rules.description: A load names the part it acts on.

rules.name: a-piece-is-held-to-what-applies-to-it
rules.expr: solve('furniture/unheld', self) == 0
rules.description: A piece in a requirement's scope (its category, and every min_<x> threshold reached) links to that requirement, so the check that requirement asks for is run.

rules.name: a-piece-stands-in-its-stability-cases
rules.expr: solve('furniture/tipping_cases', self) == 0
rules.description: Under every overturning requirement a piece links as stability_case, the static moment about its front edge keeps it standing. A prediction of the physical test the requirement describes, not a substitute for it.

rules.name: a-piece-takes-its-sideways-load
rules.expr: every(r, linked(self, 'sideways_case'), solve('furniture/sideways_margin', self, r) >= 0)
rules.description: Under every sideways requirement a piece links as sideways_case, the panels it is braced_by carry the side force: the connectors along each panel's top edge take the force in shear, those along each side edge take it in pull-out and the force times the panel's height over its width in shear, each connector good for its strength in the weaker joined material, no bearing credited (furniture/sideways_margin). A piece with no such panel is not judged to stand: its joints would have to resist bending, and no source here rates that.

rules.name: a-beam-sags-within-its-limit
rules.expr: every(r, linked(self, 'sag_limit'), solve('furniture/deflection', self) <= param(self, 'initial_share_of_longtime') * param(r, 'limit'))
rules.description: Wood Handbook Equation (9-2) with (9-3) and (9-4), through furniture/deflection: the initial deflection of a part under its own weight and the loads on it is at most the share of each sag_limit's longtime limit that creep leaves (Chapter 9, Creep Deflections).

rules.name: a-beam-is-strong-enough
rules.expr: every(c, linked(self, 'bends_as'), param(c, 'km') * 9.80665 * (solve('furniture/mass', self) + sum(params_of(backlinked(self, 'on'), 'mass'))) * param(self, 'span') * 6 / (param(self, 'depth') * param(self, 'thickness') * param(self, 'thickness')) <= param(self, 'design_bending_stress'))
rules.description: Wood Handbook Equation (9-13): the largest bending stress M/S in a part, M = km W L for its Table 9-1 case and S = b h^2/6, under its own weight and the loads on it, is at most its material's design bending stress (the near-minimum modulus of rupture over the factor for duration of load and safety). W in N, lengths in mm, stresses in MPa.

rules.name: a-part-bends-the-way-its-material-was-tested
rules.expr: every(c, linked(self, 'bends_as'), every(m, linked(self, 'uses'), payload(self, 'span_along', '') == payload(m, 'measured_along', 'unstated')))
rules.description: A part that bends spans the way its material's bending values were measured (along the grain for solid wood, face grain along the span for plywood). A material whose source does not say which way it was bent (measured_along: unstated) judges no part's bending.

rules.name: a-moving-part-stays-where-its-equation-holds
rules.expr: every(c, linked(self, 'moves_in'), len(linked(self, 'moves_per')) == 1 and solve('furniture/emc', c, 'min') >= sum(params_of(linked(self, 'moves_per'), 'mc_min')) and solve('furniture/emc', c, 'max') <= sum(params_of(linked(self, 'moves_per'), 'mc_max')))
rules.description: The movement equation a part is judged by holds over a range of moisture content (Wood Handbook Eq. 13-3: 6% to 14%); in a climate that takes the wood outside it, the movement it predicts is not to be trusted, and this says so instead of answering.

rules.name: a-moving-part-has-room-to-move
rules.expr: every(c, linked(self, 'moves_in'), param(self, payload(self, 'across_grain')) * param(self, payload(self, 'dimensional_change')) * (solve('furniture/emc', c, 'max') - solve('furniture/emc', c, 'min')) <= param(self, 'clearance'))
rules.description: Wood Handbook Eq. 13-3: across the grain a part changes by its width times its material's dimensional change coefficient times the change in moisture content between the driest and dampest air of its climate (Eq. 4-5); its clearance takes at least that.

solvers.name: furniture/deflection
solvers.description:
mm: the initial deflection of `part` under its own weight and every load `on` it,
Wood Handbook Equation (9-2) with (9-3) and (9-4): kb W L³/(E I) + ks W L/(G A′), I =
b h³/12, A′ = 5 b h/6, kb and ks from the one Table 9-1 clause the part links as
`bends_as`, L, b, h its `span`, `depth` and `thickness`, E its material's
`modulus_of_elasticity`. The shear term's G is the material property the part names in
payload `shear_modulus`. A material whose payload says its modulus is `apparent` (a
panel's bending modulus, measured on the panel with its shear deflection in it) takes no
shear term: adding one would count that deflection twice.

solvers.name: furniture/sideways_margin
solvers.description:
N: whether `piece` takes the requirement `case`'s `side_force` F across it at the
height of its top, by either of the two ways a piece of furniture does, the better
one answering:

solvers.name: furniture/emc
solvers.description:
%: the moisture content wood settles at in `climate` at its `end` ('min' or 'max'):
the climate's `temperature` (°C) and `rh_<end>` (relative humidity, a decimal), through
the equation of the clause it links as `emc_per`, whose params are W, K, K1 and K2 as
polynomials in T (`W_0`, `W_1`, `W_2`, ...). Wood Handbook Equation (4-5).

solvers.name: furniture/height
solvers.description: mm: from the floor to the top of the highest part.

solvers.name: furniture/overturning_margin
solvers.description:
N·mm: the moment holding the piece down about its front tipping edge, minus the one
tipping it, under the test conditions the requirement `case` states — its params
`tilt_block` (mm, the rear supports raised so the piece leans forward), `point_mass`
(kg on the front top edge of an open extendible element, each in turn, the worst one
kept), and `fill_density` with `fill_share` (kg/m3 of storage volume in every
extendible element, when they hold at least that share of the piece's
`storage_volume`). Every extendible element is open. Positive: it stays standing.

solvers.name: furniture/tipping_cases
solvers.description:
How many of the requirements `piece` links as `stability_case` it is predicted to
tip under.

solvers.name: furniture/unheld
solvers.description: How many requirements apply to `piece` (in_scope) that it does not link to.

payload.quote: Clothing storage unit means any free-standing furniture item manufactured in the United States or imported for use in the United States that is intended for the storage of clothing, typical of bedroom furniture.
Each clothing storage unit that is subject to ASTM F2057-23, Standard Safety Specification for Clothing Storage Units, approved on February 1, 2023, shall comply with ASTM F2057-23.
Testing of all clothing storage units as specified by the Commission, including those 27 inches and above in height
The ASTM standard excludes units weighing less than 30 pounds empty.

Staff therefore concluded that the Commission could find that, based on tip-over data, testing units having a storage volume less than 3.2 cubic feet is not ``reasonably necessary'' to protect children from injury or death.

fr.name: Scie égoïne
method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

fr.name: Scie à guichet

Scier du côté chute du trait.

en.name: Keyhole saw
method: Drill a hole in the waste large enough to admit the point of the saw.
Insert the blade and start slowly, with a minimum of pressure; do not twist it sharply, the narrow blade bends easily.
Saw on the waste side of the line.

fr.name: Scie égoïne
method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

fr.name: Scie égoïne
method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.

fr.name: Scie égoïne
method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

Scier du côté chute du trait.

en.name: Keyhole saw
method: Drill a hole in the waste large enough to admit the point of the saw.
Insert the blade and start slowly, with a minimum of pressure; do not twist it sharply, the narrow blade bends easily.
Saw on the waste side of the line.

payload.quote: Clothing storage unit means any free-standing furniture item manufactured in the United States or imported for use in the United States that is intended for the storage of clothing, typical of bedroom furniture.
Each clothing storage unit that is subject to ASTM F2057-23, Standard Safety Specification for Clothing Storage Units, approved on February 1, 2023, shall comply with ASTM F2057-23.
Testing of all clothing storage units as specified by the Commission, including those 27 inches and above in height
The ASTM standard excludes units weighing less than 30 pounds empty.

Staff therefore concluded that the Commission could find that, based on tip-over data, testing units having a storage volume less than 3.2 cubic feet is not ``reasonably necessary'' to protect children from injury or death.

fr.name: Scie égoïne
method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

fr.name: Scie à guichet
method: Percer dans la chute un trou assez grand pour y engager la pointe de la scie.

Scier du côté chute du trait.

en.name: Keyhole saw
method: Drill a hole in the waste large enough to admit the point of the saw.
Insert the blade and start slowly, with a minimum of pressure; do not twist it sharply, the narrow blade bends easily.
Saw on the waste side of the line.

fr.name: Scie égoïne
method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

fr.name: Scie à guichet

Scier du côté chute du trait.

en.name: Keyhole saw
method: Drill a hole in the waste large enough to admit the point of the saw.
Insert the blade and start slowly, with a minimum of pressure; do not twist it sharply, the narrow blade bends easily.

Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

fr.name: Scie égoïne
method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

fr.name: Scie à guichet
method: Percer dans la chute un trou assez grand pour y engager la pointe de la scie.
Engager la lame et commencer doucement, sans forcer ; ne pas la tordre, elle plie facilement.
Scier du côté chute du trait.

en.name: Keyhole saw
method: Drill a hole in the waste large enough to admit the point of the saw.
Insert the blade and start slowly, with a minimum of pressure; do not twist it sharply, the narrow blade bends easily.
Saw on the waste side of the line.

payload.quote: Clothing storage unit means any free-standing furniture item manufactured in the United States or imported for use in the United States that is intended for the storage of clothing, typical of bedroom furniture.
Each clothing storage unit that is subject to ASTM F2057-23, Standard Safety Specification for Clothing Storage Units, approved on February 1, 2023, shall comply with ASTM F2057-23.
Testing of all clothing storage units as specified by the Commission, including those 27 inches and above in height
The ASTM standard excludes units weighing less than 30 pounds empty.

Staff therefore concluded that the Commission could find that, based on tip-over data, testing units having a storage volume less than 3.2 cubic feet is not ``reasonably necessary'' to protect children from injury or death.

payload.quote: Section 9.2.1 of the ASTM standard, Simulated Clothing Load, is a test conducted on a hard, level, and flat test surface with extendible elements and doors open and, if 50 percent or more of the storage volume is extended, the unit is to be filled with a ``simulated clothing load.'' The fill weight in extendible elements is calculated using a density of 8.5 pounds per cubic foot of volume

fr.name: Scie égoïne
method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

payload.does: saws a cut that starts inside the board, from a drilled hole

fr.name: Scie à guichet
method: Percer dans la chute un trou assez grand pour y engager la pointe de la scie.
Engager la lame et commencer doucement, sans forcer ; ne pas la tordre, elle plie facilement.
Scier du côté chute du trait.

en.name: Keyhole saw
method: Drill a hole in the waste large enough to admit the point of the saw.
Insert the blade and start slowly, with a minimum of pressure; do not twist it sharply, the narrow blade bends easily.
Saw on the waste side of the line.

payload.quote: Clothing storage unit means any free-standing furniture item manufactured in the United States or imported for use in the United States that is intended for the storage of clothing, typical of bedroom furniture.
Each clothing storage unit that is subject to ASTM F2057-23, Standard Safety Specification for Clothing Storage Units, approved on February 1, 2023, shall comply with ASTM F2057-23.
Testing of all clothing storage units as specified by the Commission, including those 27 inches and above in height
The ASTM standard excludes units weighing less than 30 pounds empty.

Staff therefore concluded that the Commission could find that, based on tip-over data, testing units having a storage volume less than 3.2 cubic feet is not ``reasonably necessary'' to protect children from injury or death.

payload.locator: Preamble II.B, describing ASTM F2057-23 section 9.2.1, 88 FR 28405
payload.quote: Section 9.2.1 of the ASTM standard, Simulated Clothing Load, is a test conducted on a hard, level, and flat test surface with extendible elements and doors open and, if 50 percent or more of the storage volume is extended, the unit is to be filled with a ``simulated clothing load.'' The fill weight in extendible elements is calculated using a density of 8.5 pounds per cubic foot of volume
All extendible elements are opened and must remain open for 30 seconds without tip over.

fr.name: Scie égoïne
method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

Scier du côté chute du trait.

en.name: Keyhole saw

fr.name: Scie égoïne
method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

fr.name: Scie à guichet
method: Percer dans la chute un trou assez grand pour y engager la pointe de la scie.
Engager la lame et commencer doucement, sans forcer ; ne pas la tordre, elle plie facilement.
Scier du côté chute du trait.

en.name: Keyhole saw
method: Drill a hole in the waste large enough to admit the point of the saw.
Insert the blade and start slowly, with a minimum of pressure; do not twist it sharply, the narrow blade bends easily.
Saw on the waste side of the line.

fr.name: Scie égoïne
method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

fr.name: Scie à guichet
method: Percer dans la chute un trou assez grand pour y engager la pointe de la scie.
Engager la lame et commencer doucement, sans forcer ; ne pas la tordre, elle plie facilement.
Scier du côté chute du trait.

en.name: Keyhole saw
method: Drill a hole in the waste large enough to admit the point of the saw.
Insert the blade and start slowly, with a minimum of pressure; do not twist it sharply, the narrow blade bends easily.
Saw on the waste side of the line.

payload.quote: Clothing storage unit means any free-standing furniture item manufactured in the United States or imported for use in the United States that is intended for the storage of clothing, typical of bedroom furniture.
Each clothing storage unit that is subject to ASTM F2057-23, Standard Safety Specification for Clothing Storage Units, approved on February 1, 2023, shall comply with ASTM F2057-23.
Testing of all clothing storage units as specified by the Commission, including those 27 inches and above in height
The ASTM standard excludes units weighing less than 30 pounds empty.

Staff therefore concluded that the Commission could find that, based on tip-over data, testing units having a storage volume less than 3.2 cubic feet is not ``reasonably necessary'' to protect children from injury or death.

The fill weight in extendible elements is calculated using a density of 8.5 pounds per cubic foot of volume

fr.name: Scie égoïne
method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

fr.name: Scie à guichet
method: Percer dans la chute un trou assez grand pour y engager la pointe de la scie.
Engager la lame et commencer doucement, sans forcer ; ne pas la tordre, elle plie facilement.
Scier du côté chute du trait.

en.name: Keyhole saw
method: Drill a hole in the waste large enough to admit the point of the saw.
Insert the blade and start slowly, with a minimum of pressure; do not twist it sharply, the narrow blade bends easily.
Saw on the waste side of the line.

children.name: Safety Standard for Clothing Storage Units, direct final rule, 88 FR 28403 (16 CFR part 1261)

payload.publisher: U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, Federal Register
payload.capture: sources/federal-register-2023-08997/2023-08997.txt
payload.note: The rule adopts ASTM F2057-23 by reference; its test methods are ASTM's and copyrighted. What is quoted here is the Commission's public description of them.

payload.quote: Clothing storage unit means any free-standing furniture item manufactured in the United States or imported for use in the United States that is intended for the storage of clothing, typical of bedroom furniture.
Each clothing storage unit that is subject to ASTM F2057-23, Standard Safety Specification for Clothing Storage Units, approved on February 1, 2023, shall comply with ASTM F2057-23.
Testing of all clothing storage units as specified by the Commission, including those 27 inches and above in height
The ASTM standard excludes units weighing less than 30 pounds empty.

Staff therefore concluded that the Commission could find that, based on tip-over data, testing units having a storage volume less than 3.2 cubic feet is not ``reasonably necessary'' to protect children from injury or death.

payload.locator: Preamble II.B, describing ASTM F2057-23 section 9.2.1, 88 FR 28405
payload.quote: Section 9.2.1 of the ASTM standard, Simulated Clothing Load, is a test conducted on a hard, level, and flat test surface with extendible elements and doors open and, if 50 percent or more of the storage volume is extended, the unit is to be filled with a ``simulated clothing load.'' The fill weight in extendible elements is calculated using a density of 8.5 pounds per cubic foot of volume

fr.name: Scie égoïne
method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

Scier du côté chute du trait.

en.name: Keyhole saw

method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

fr.name: Scie égoïne
method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

fr.name: Scie à guichet
method: Percer dans la chute un trou assez grand pour y engager la pointe de la scie.
Engager la lame et commencer doucement, sans forcer ; ne pas la tordre, elle plie facilement.
Scier du côté chute du trait.

en.name: Keyhole saw
method: Drill a hole in the waste large enough to admit the point of the saw.
Insert the blade and start slowly, with a minimum of pressure; do not twist it sharply, the narrow blade bends easily.
Saw on the waste side of the line.

payload.quote: Clothing storage unit means any free-standing furniture item manufactured in the United States or imported for use in the United States that is intended for the storage of clothing, typical of bedroom furniture.
Each clothing storage unit that is subject to ASTM F2057-23, Standard Safety Specification for Clothing Storage Units, approved on February 1, 2023, shall comply with ASTM F2057-23.
Testing of all clothing storage units as specified by the Commission, including those 27 inches and above in height

The temperature and time a board on sale was treated at are its maker's and are unknown here. Borůvka et al. (2018) measured clear beech at 102.7 MPa mean bending strength untreated, 108.8 after 165 °C and 42.0 after 210 °C: a board treated hotter than 190 °C may be much weaker than this.
payload.note: Graded boards with knots, not clear wood: a shelf of selected lamellas may be stronger. Treated boards scatter far more than untreated ones (coefficient of variation 45% against 14%), which the characteristic strength takes in.

Crosscut saw

payload.does: saws a straight cut that starts at an edge of the board

fr.name: Scie égoïne
method: Scier du côté chute du trait, pour ne pas raccourcir la pièce de l'épaisseur de la coupe.
Amorcer en tirant la scie vers soi quelques fois par le talon, le pouce contre la lame, bien au-dessus des dents.
Scier en poussant seulement, la scie à environ 45°, sans forcer ; garder la lame d'équerre à la face, en la vérifiant de temps en temps à l'équerre.
En fin de coupe, tenir la chute pour qu'elle ne casse pas en arrachant le bord.

en.name: Crosscut saw
method: Saw on the waste side of the line, so the part is not cut short by the thickness of the cut.
Start by drawing the saw back a few times at its heel, your thumb against the blade well above the teeth.
Saw only on the downward stroke, at about 45°, pressing evenly; keep the blade at a right angle to the face, checking it now and then with a try square.
Near the end of each cut, hold the waste so it does not break off unevenly.

children.name: Keyhole saw

payload.does: saws a cut that starts inside the board, from a drilled hole

fr.name: Scie à guichet
method: Percer dans la chute un trou assez grand pour y engager la pointe de la scie.
Engager la lame et commencer doucement, sans forcer ; ne pas la tordre, elle plie facilement.
Scier du côté chute du trait.

en.name: Keyhole saw
method: Drill a hole in the waste large enough to admit the point of the saw.
Insert the blade and start slowly, with a minimum of pressure; do not twist it sharply, the narrow blade bends easily.
Saw on the waste side of the line.
